logs.scenario: Ordering integrity check — Step 2 before Step 3
logs.description: adversarial MJWT has both alg:none AND an invalid signature. Verifier MUST report MJWT_ALG_INVALID (Step 2), never reach or report MJWT_SIGNATURE_INVALID (Step 3) — confirms short-circuit ordering, not just correct final verdict.

logs.scenario: Ordering integrity check — Step 1 before Step 3
logs.description: adversarial MJWT has both aud mismatch AND an invalid signature. Verifier MUST report MJWT_AUD_MISMATCH (Step 1) without expending cryptographic resources on signature verification — the draft's stated rationale for the Step 1 -> Step 3 ordering (timing side-channel resistance).

Root Mandate is revoked (added to Revocation Registry) after a Child Mandate was issued and previously verified against it. Presenting the same, otherwise-untampered Child Mandate again MUST now fail at Step 9 with NARROWING_VIOLATION — a cached/previously-verified parent object is not sufficient; live re-verification against the Revocation Registry catches it. Confirms MJWT-04 Section 8.1 Step 9 / Section 11.8 (PEDIGREE 'parent-swap' defense).

logs.scenario: NARROWING_VIOLATION — parent-swap via signature no longer verifying [NEW in -04]
logs.description: Root Mandate's signature no longer verifies against the issuer key presented at Step 9 (simulates key rotation/compromise since the parent was first issued). Child Mandate is otherwise valid and untampered. Verifier MUST reject with NARROWING_VIOLATION at Step 9 rather than trusting a previously-decoded parent claims object — confirms live signature re-verification, distinct from and in addition to the revocation check (E-22).
